Time: 2 min. Teaching intent: Open the hour and connect it to the week's decision.
Talk track: Use hard rules, electrical behavior, process constraints, and traceable evidence to choose a route.
Expected answer / misconception: Students can name the outcome.
Visual: The visual previews the physical design or evidence chain.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Set the evidence contract.
Talk track: A candidate comparison with a legal route, unresolved risk, and next verification step.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Should A win because its route is shorter?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Resolve the hard violation before comparing performance.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A layout that violates width, space, via, or assembly rules cannot be ranked as ready by a softer performance metric. Trace the visual in order: design rule; candidate status; repair action. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic A is shorter but crosses a forbidden keep-out; B is longer and legal. Record A as requiring redesign before SI ranking. Boundary: The route comparison is synthetic teaching data.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R3: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 22: Interconnects | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch22_2D-3D.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Synthetic A is shorter but crosses a forbidden keep-out; B is longer and legal. Record A as requiring redesign before SI ranking. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. The route comparison is synthetic teaching data.
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.

R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf

Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: The selection record includes source, rule version, route revision, model output definition, uncertainty, and a reviewer-visible reason. Trace the visual in order: source / revision; rule check; next evidence. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: A peer redraws one path and verifies every claimed rule from the brief. Any unverified rule remains open.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
